# Code 
Quarto supports executable code, code examples, and syntax-highlighted snippets for a wide range of programming languages. This makes it ideal for creating teaching materials, laboratory manuals, lecture notes, and technical documentation.

## Including inline code snippets
You can include inline code snippets in between backticks, e.g. ` ```print("Hello, world!")``` `.

## Including code blocks
You can include code blocks in triple backticks, followed by the language name (for syntax highlighting) e.g.
` ```python`

` print("Hello, world!")`

` ``` `

This results in the following rendered code output:
```python
import numpy as np
print("Hello, world!")
```

::: {.callout-tip}

Supported languages for syntax highlighting include: Python, R, Bash, C, C++, Java, JavaScript, MATLAB, markdown and many more. See the [Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/code.html#code-blocks) for a full list of supported languages.

For completely unformatted text use the ` ```text` option.

:::



### Running Code

Executable code is placed inside a code chunk (notice the curly braces after the opening triple backticks). You can specify the programming language for the code chunk (e.g. `python`, `r`, `julia`, `bash`, etc.) and Quarto will automatically highlight the syntax.

` ```{python}`

` #| eval: false`

` print("Hello, world!")`

` ``` `

This results in the following rendered output (shows code and output):

::: {.cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
print("Hello, world!")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
Hello, world!
```
:::
:::


## Showing Output but Hiding Code
You can run the code and display the output  but hide the code source from viewers with `#| echo: false`


` ```{python}`

` #| echo: false`

` print("Only the output will appear.")`

` ``` `

This results in the following rendered output:

::: {.cell execution_count=2}

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
Only the output will appear.
```
:::
:::


## Folding Long Code Blocks

Long code examples can be collapsed to avoid cluttering the document with `#| code-fold: true`. You can also add a summary to the code block with `#| code-summary: "Show Python code"`.

` ```{python} `

` #| code-fold: true`

` #| code-summary: "Show Python code" `

` `

`print("This code is initially hidden.")`

` ``` `

::: {.cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Show Python code"}
print("This code is initially hidden.")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
This code is initially hidden.
```
:::
:::


::: {.callout-note}

The folding code blocks are expanded in the static PDF output.

:::


::: {.callout-tip}

It's a good idea to keep code lines short (e.g. < 80 characters) as the LaTeX output does not wrap long lines of code.

:::


## Figures from code {#sec-code-figs}

Figures generated from Python, R, or Julia code are **automatically** treated as figures. You should include:

 - `#| label: fig-line-plot` - this gives a reference label to the figure
 - `#| fig-cap: "A simple line plot"` - this gives a figure caption
 - `#| fig-alt: "Descriptive alt text"` - this gives alternative text for accessibility (e.g. screen readers)
  
` ```{python} `

`#| label: fig-line-plot`

`#| fig-cap: "A simple line plot"`

`#| fig-alt: "Line graph showing values increasing and decreasing across four observations."`

`import matplotlib.pyplot as plt`

`plt.plot([1, 23, 2, 4])`

`plt.show()`

` ``` `

::: {.cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.plot([1, 23, 2, 4])
plt.show()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![A simple line plot](code_files/figure-docx/fig-line-plot-output-1.png){#fig-line-plot fig-alt='Line graph showing values increasing and decreasing across four observations.'}
:::
:::


::: {.callout-tip}

Often it's useful to add  `#| echo: false` at the start of the figure will make sure to not echo the code and only display the figure:

` ```{python}`

`#| echo: false`

`#| label: fig-line-plot-noecho`

`#| fig-cap: "A simple line plot"`

`#| fig-alt: "A simplified plot with the `#| echo: false` to not show the code"`

`import matplotlib.pyplot as plt`

`plt.plot([1, 23, 2, 4])`

`plt.show()`

` ``` `

::: {.cell execution_count=5}

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![A simple line plot](code_files/figure-docx/fig-line-plot-noecho-output-1.png){#fig-line-plot-noecho fig-alt='A simplified plot with the `#| echo: false` to not show the code'}
:::
:::


:::



## Global Code Options

Chunk options can be applied to every code block using the document YAML.

````markdown
---
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---
````
